title: The Boat and the Stars
translation: Just as a man in a boat moving forward sees the still objects on the shore moving backward, so at Lanka (on the equator) the still stars are seen moving exactly westward.
translation_hi: जैसे आगे बढ़ती नाव में बैठा व्यक्ति किनारे की स्थिर वस्तुओं को पीछे की ओर जाते देखता है, वैसे ही लंका (भूमध्य रेखा) पर स्थिर तारे ठीक पश्चिम की ओर जाते दिखाई देते हैं।
question: A point on the equator travels about 40,075 km in 24 hours. Roughly how fast is it moving, in km/h?
solution:
Speed = 40075 km / 24 h ≈ 1670 km/h

We feel none of it, just as the man in the smooth boat feels still while the shore slides past.

Science link: Aryabhata explained the daily motion of the stars by the Earth's rotation, about a thousand years before Copernicus. Relative motion, the boat analogy, is the same idea Galileo used and Einstein built relativity on. Many later Indian astronomers rejected this view, so Aryabhata was ahead even of his own tradition.
